fatal_errors: The proposed route concerns precipitation-strengthened tungsten-based refractory alloys rather than the target lamellar Al0.7CoCrFeNi eutectic high-entropy alloy.
It replaces the defining 6 GPa, 1473 K, 2-hour HPHT intervention with an unspecified multistage thermo-mechanical treatment.
The proposed coherent nanoprecipitation mechanism does not reconstruct the target transformation to hierarchical FCC/B2 patterns with coherent interfaces and interphase dislocation transfer.
The baseline compares against single-principal-element alloys instead of the untreated or conventionally processed eutectic alloy.
The falsification experiment lacks pressure-matched and temperature-time-matched controls and does not measure interface coherence, GND-density convergence, deformation modes, or crack morphology.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad strength–ductility objective and cites evidence that a specific W–Ni–Fe–Ta refractory multi-principal-element alloy can attain approximately 2 GPa yield strength and 15% uniform ductility through coherent precipitation. It is therefore a scientifically plausible alternative for that different alloy system. However, it does not reconstruct the target material, HPHT conditions, hierarchical FCC/B2 structural evolution, interfacial dislocation-transfer mechanism, or the reported approximately 1150 MPa and 36% response. Evidence E2 supports the alternative composition directly, while E1 and E3 provide only broader context; none establishes that this route applies to the brittle Al0.7CoCrFeNi eutectic family. The proposed mechanical-property comparison is also weakly discriminating because it cannot separate the claimed precipitation mechanism from ordinary thermal or strain-history effects.
